provenance.source: qmint.protocols.wiesner (lane B) + qmint.quantum (lane F) + qmint.proofs (lane D)

protocol.verifier_rule: measure every qubit in its secret basis; accept iff wrong positions ≤ threshold

flow.label: Bank mints the note
flow.detail: 5 qubits, each one of |0⟩ |1⟩ |+⟩ |−⟩ chosen uniformly; the bank keeps the choice secret

flow.label: Holder stores / sends it
flow.detail: ideal channel: nothing disturbs the qubits

flow.label: Bank verifies (spend once)
flow.detail: each qubit measured in its secret basis; at most 1 mismatches allowed; one sampled verification (the note is consumed)

flow.label: Same serial presented again
flow.detail: bank ledger: serial is 'spent'; replay refused without measuring

flow.label: Bank issues a fresh note
flow.detail: accepted notes are replaced by a new note with a new serial

circuit.bit_order_note: qubit q_i is Qiskit qubit i, measured into clbit i; outcomes are shown in C7 order (char i = q_i)

acceptance.label: Honest acceptance, this note (bank exact)
acceptance.note: bank-side analysis oracle; cross-checked against the lane-F closed form to 1e-9

statistics.error_counts_note: number of wrong positions in one verification of this note; per-position results are never returned (they would reveal the secret)

theorem.label: W2 theorem bound
theorem.note: game W2 (threshold verifier): no published closed-form bound; (3/4)^n does NOT transfer

hardware.label: Quantum hardware
hardware.note: not run: paid hardware submission is disabled in this build (lane J); no QPU number exists

teaching.warning: TEST_ONLY teaching reveal: the bank's leak_secret_TEST_ONLY control was called because you asked for it. A real issuer never discloses bases or bits; with them a trivial forger wins every time (OUT_OF_MODEL).

circuit.bit_order_note: qubit q_i is Qiskit qubit i, measured into clbit i; outcomes are shown in C7 order (char i = q_i)

generic_transpile.note: generic CX+1q basis, NOT hardware-native gate counts

data.simulator_caveat: A simulator's state is classical data that can be copied freely; nothing here demonstrates physical no-cloning. Only the modelled quantum register is simulated.
